title: Torch Radar: short vignettes & reading radar
content:
Quick radar: spring 2026 sink-in notes and micro-actions

Top-line summary:
- Short vignettes from papers + workshop. Focus: low-latency long-context primitives (sparsity + micro-batching), quantization stability tricks for decoder-only models, and a small runtime kernel-fusion idea that might save 5-12% token latency on seq lengths > 2k.
- This doc is intentionally terse: quick take, why it matters for Redwood Inference, and tiny experiments to try on our Dedicated pools.

Papers & short takes (my reading shorthand)
1) "Block-sparse cross-attention for streaming long contexts" (arXiv 2604.01234)
   - gist: break cross-attn into overlapping blocks, allow O(n sqrt(n)) work with local dense windows plus sparse global hops. Uses deterministic routing to maintain KV cache locality.
   - why it matters: could reduce effective KV memory pressure while keeping per-token latency steady for long sessions. If routing deterministic -> caching easier to shard across GPUs.
   - immediate micro-experiment: implement a reference block-sparse attention wrapper around our llama-like runtime (python prototype) and run on 8k synthetic sessions to measure throughput vs baseline. Tag: EXP-quant-kv-001 (internal sandbox).
   - open question: interaction with prefix caching policies — do we need new eviction heuristics (LRU -> hop-frequency-aware)?

2) "Layer-wise scale-adaptive quantization for decoder-only LLMs"
   - gist: per-layer learned scale factors that are constrained during finetune to improve Post-quantization stability (8->4 bit). Authors show reduced perplexity degradation and fewer generation artifacts.
   - why it matters: Redwood Optimize could recommend safer quant profiles for customer workloads. For Dedicated, this might mean offering a "conservative low-bit" option that preserves quality on chat-heavy workloads.
   - tiny test: pick 6 SFT datasets, apply proposed scaling, quantize to 4-bit, and compare ngram-level regressions + a small human eval (3 labelers) on hallucination rate. Use our eval harness: /evals/quant-stability/runner.
   - note: watch for per-token latency anomalies; scale compensation sometimes increases compute in-float fallback in their code path.

3) "Micro-kernel fusion for causal decoding" (conference poster)
   - gist: fuse KV lookup + update + softmax into one CUDA kernel for small heads/medium dims; authors claim 5-12% latency drop for seq length >2k. Implementation complexity moderate.
   - why it matters: direct win for long-chat customers where latency SLOs are tight. Could be a low-cost performance layer for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.
   - experiment: port their CUDA kernel to our runtime (start with a CPU fallback test) and benchmark on p4d and a local V100 rig. PR: draft branch rf/kernel-fusion-experiments.

4) "Adaptive request batching with early-cutoff"
   - gist: scheduler that opportunistically batches in-flight requests but has an "early cutoff" for high-priority low-latency tokens. Uses a tiny RL signal to tune cutoff.
   - why it matters: aligns to Redwood's thesis: make serving cost predictable while preserving tail latency. Could integrate into smart routing as a per-customer policy.
   - to test: instrument our serving layer with a synthetic workload that mixes 95% batchable traffic + 5% p99 interactive traffic and compare cost/SLO curves vs current fixed-batch policy.

Workshop & conference notes (Inference Ops workshop, 2026-05)
- Panel on graceful degradation: operators prefer deterministic fallback chains (model variant -> region -> capacity-tier) rather than probabilistic rollouts in SRE contexts. Good signal for product: expose deterministic fallback policy templates in Console rollouts UI.
- Talk: "observability for unit economics" — speaker suggested token-level causal tracing (token->kernel->queue) for chargeback. We should prototype token-level traces for 10% of requests to avoid cost blowup.
- Interesting hack: one team uses a tiny LLM surrogate to predict whether a request will be costly (large context + complex decode) and routes those to a cost-optimized model. Consider a lightweight classifier as a routing hook.

Bookmarks & short links
- block-sparse paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01234
- micro-kernel repo (example): https://github.com/example/kernel-fusion-demo
- RL-batcher paper notes: https://docs.google.com/paper-notes (placeholder)
- internal PR for kv-cache experiments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/42

To-do / next micro-tasks (prioritized)
- [ ] Spin up EXP-quant-kv-001 sandbox (owner: Michael) -> create dataset + synthetic long sessions, due 2026-05-19. Linked ticket: JIRA-ILM-1287.
- [ ] Kernel-fusion prototype: get a single fused kernel running against existing runtime (owner: Keira), due 2026-05-25. Create draft PR and perf notes.
- [ ] Small eval: 4-bit layer-scale tests on 3 SFTs (owner: Ivy), add to quant-stability harness. Due 2026-06-01.
- [ ] Design doc: "fallback-policy templates" for Console (owner: Michael + product), very rough draft by 2026-05-30. Link to Confluence after initial sketch.

Notes-to-self (scratchpad)
- Watch out for evaluation leakage: when testing low-bit configs, keep eval prompts separate (no train-overlap).
- Quick heuristic: if quantization reduces top-1 token probability mass by > 0.03 on anchor prompts, mark as "unsafe" for chat workloads. (Tweak threshold later.)
- Consider feasibility of offering "policy presets" in Console: conservative-lowbit, aggressive-lowbit, latency-first. Map presets to: quant profile + batching strategy + routing hint.

Random fragments / thoughts
- Maybe reuse the RL-batcher idea as a CLI knob for Dedicated: customers can enable "predictive batching" with a defined p99 SLA tolerance.
- If block-sparse routing is deterministic, eviction heuristics could be computed offline and shipped as small hints in model metadata (cheap to store).

References & cross-links (internal)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OPS/Inference-Runtime-Playbook
- GH sandbox: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments
- Eval harness path: /evals/quant-stability/runner (internal repo)

End of quick radar.

Notes: this is deliberately terse. Will expand into a longer doc if any micro-experiment shows promise.
